api.notes: Optional: without it the field wires the control it finds (the first native control, or the group container for `group-label`).
Labels a group (radio group, fieldset-like container) with `role=group` and `aria-labelledby`; a click on the label does not forward.
The control. Its label, description and status are light-DOM satellites next to it, so aria-labelledby and aria-describedby resolve without crossing a shadow root.
Shows an info-tip button after the label. See FIELD-04.
Object `{type, message?, messageID?}`, or the `status-type` and `status-message` attributes; `messageID` is `status-id`.
A number is px, a string a CSS length. Not reflected.

api.reason: React refs. The element itself is the reference.

hooks.notes: Light mode of the shared chrome controller (packages/core/src/controllers/field-chrome.ts); tct-text-input uses its shadow mode. The field also provides `fieldContext` to nested controls.

keyboard.keys: Click on the label or the description
keyboard.action: Focuses (or activates) the control, as a real <label for> does; not over a nested link or button, not while text is selected.

form.notes: The wrapped control owns the form value. A wrapped tct-* control gets the error state pushed to it when `status-type` is error, so aria-invalid and :state(user-invalid) show without a submit attempt.

differences.text: The label, description and status are owned satellites in the light DOM of the field (`data-tct-owned`, slots label, description and status), not shadow-DOM children, so the wrapped control's aria-labelledby and aria-describedby reference them in one tree (A-18). Do not slot your own elements with those names.
`input-id` is optional: the field finds the control itself and gives it an id when it has none.
The label does not turn pink on focus (the Tecton field only draws the focus ring on the box), and the status is coloured ink with no wash behind it.
The label tooltip is a focusable info button with an accessible name ("More information"), so keyboard and touch users can open it; upstream shows it on the label icon only.

A horizontal-labels form layout (`data-horizontal-labels`, published by the form layout context) lets the host disappear so the parent grid places label and control. The label context of an input group needs an element from WP-7 and is not wired yet.

requests.reason: Edited as an assigned core file: `ids` overrides (label, description, status ids) and an `indicator` attribute on the label satellite. Listed so the orchestrator knows the controller changed shape.

core.field.notes: Guides: [mwg:accessible-error-announcement] the status is announced once, politely, through the announcer; [mwg:required-field-feedback] required and optional indicators are text, not colour; [mwg:validate-input-after-interaction] errors show after interaction; [mwg:accessible-web-components] id references stay in one tree; [mwg:form-associated-custom-elements] wrapped tct-* controls stay the form participants.

api.notes: The default slot takes rich label text instead.

api.reason: `id` is a global attribute; tct-field gives the label satellite its id (or `label-id`).
The description is a separate satellite (tct-field-description) whose id is `description-id` on tct-field; the label only renders the text.

hooks.notes: The form layout's optionality default decides whether the Required or Optional indicator shows.

keyboard.action: Forwards to the control named by `input-id` (see Field).

differences.text: Mostly internal: tct-field and tct-text-input create it as an owned satellite. An `indicator` attribute (internal) carries the resolved Required/Optional text for the satellite.

core.field-label.notes: Guides: [mwg:required-field-feedback] the indicator is text ("Required" or "Optional") beside the label, not a colour.

api.notes: Accessible name and tooltip, such as "Clear Search".
Native click retargeted from the inner button; one per activation.

keyboard.action: Activates it (a native button); tct-text-input clears, fires input and change, and restores focus to the input synchronously.

differences.text: A native button with a tct-icon and a tct-tooltip in the shadow root, not a tct-button: the box is the small square Tecton draws inside an input. A pointer press never takes focus from the input, and on coarse pointers the hit area grows to 24px.

core.input-clear-button.notes: Guides: [mwg:custom-button-actions] a real button, activated by keyboard and pointer alike.
